verses.1:1: The oracle of the word of the LORD to Israel by the hand of Malachi.
verses.1:2: "I have loved you," says the LORD. Yet you say, "In what manner have You loved us?" "Was not Esau Jacob's brother?" declares the LORD. "Yet I have loved Jacob,
verses.1:3: but Esau I have hated; I have laid his mountains desolate and given his heritage to the jackals of the wilderness."
verses.1:4: Though Edom says, "We have been shattered, yet we will return and rebuild the ruins," thus says the LORD of hosts: "They may build, but I will tear down; and they shall be called 'The Territory of Wickedness,' and 'The People with whom the LORD is indignant forever.'"
verses.1:5: Your own eyes shall see it, and you yourselves shall say, "Great is the LORD beyond the territory of Israel!"
verses.1:6: "A son honors a father, and a servant his master. If then I am a father, where is My honor? And if I am a master, where is My reverence?" says the LORD of hosts to you, O priests who despise My name. "Yet you say, 'In what way have we despised Your name?'
verses.1:7: By presenting defiled food upon My altar! Yet you say, 'In what way have we defiled You?' By saying, 'The table of the LORD is to be despised.'
verses.1:8: And when you present the blind for sacrifice, is it not evil? And when you present the lame and the sick, is it not evil? Offer it now to your governor! Will he be pleased with you, or will he receive you favorably?" says the LORD of hosts.
verses.1:9: And now, implore the favor of God, that He may be gracious to us! "With such a thing coming from your hand, will He receive any of you favorably?" says the LORD of hosts.
verses.1:10: "Oh, that there were even one among you who would shut the doors, so that you would not kindle fire on My altar in vain! I have no delight in you," says the LORD of hosts, "nor will I accept an offering from your hand.
verses.1:11: For from the rising of the sun even to its setting, My name is great among the nations; and in every place incense is presented to My name, and a pure offering; for great is My name among the nations," says the LORD of hosts.
verses.1:12: "But you profane it by saying, 'The table of the Lord is defiled, and its produce, even its food, is to be despised.'
verses.1:13: You also say, 'Behold, what a weariness!' and you snort at it," says the LORD of hosts. "And you bring what was taken by violence, and the lame, and the sick; thus you bring the offering! Shall I accept that from your hand?" says the LORD.
verses.1:14: "Cursed be the deceiver who has a male in his flock, and makes a vow, yet sacrifices to the Lord what is blemished; for I am a great King," says the LORD of hosts, "and My name is feared among the nations."
verses.2:1: "And now, for you is this commandment, O priests.
verses.2:2: If you will not listen, and if you will not take it to heart to give glory to My name," says the LORD of hosts, "then I will send the curse upon you, and I will curse your blessings; indeed, I have already cursed them, because you do not lay it to heart.
verses.2:3: Behold, I will rebuke your seed, and I will spread dung upon your faces, the dung of your solemn feasts; and one shall carry you away with it.
verses.2:4: Then you shall know that I have sent this command to you, so that My covenant with Levi may endure," says the LORD of hosts.
verses.2:5: "My covenant with him was one of life and peace, and I gave them to him for reverence, and he revered Me and stood in awe before My name.
verses.2:6: The law of truth was in his mouth, and no perversity was found on his lips; he walked with Me in peace and uprightness, and he turned many back from iniquity.
verses.2:7: For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and men should seek the law from his mouth; for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts.
verses.2:8: But you have turned aside from the way; you have caused many to stumble at the law; you have corrupted the covenant of Levi," says the LORD of hosts.
verses.2:9: "Therefore I also have made you despised and brought low before all the people, just as you do not keep My ways, but show partiality in the law."
verses.2:10: Do we not all have one Father? Has not one God created us? Why do we deal treacherously each man against his brother, profaning the covenant of our fathers?
verses.2:11: Judah has dealt treacherously, and an abomination has been committed in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah has profaned the sanctuary of the LORD, which He loves, and has married the daughter of a foreign god.
verses.2:12: May the LORD cut off from the tents of Jacob, for the man who does this, both him who wakes and him who answers, even though he presents an offering to the LORD of hosts!
verses.2:13: And this second thing you do: you cover the altar of the LORD with tears, with weeping and groaning, because He no longer regards the offering nor receives it with favor from your hand.
verses.2:14: Yet you say, "For what reason?" Because the LORD has been witness between you and the wife of your youth, against whom you have dealt treacherously, though she is your companion and the wife of your covenant.
verses.2:15: Did He not make them one, with a remnant of the Spirit belonging to Him? And why one? He seeks godly offspring. Therefore guard your spirit, and let none deal treacherously with the wife of his youth.
verses.2:16: For the LORD, the God of Israel, says that He hates divorce, and him who covers his garment with violence, says the LORD of hosts. Therefore guard your spirit, and do not deal treacherously.
verses.2:17: You have wearied the LORD with your words. Yet you say, "In what way have we wearied Him?" By your saying, "Everyone who does evil is good in the sight of the LORD, and in them He delights," or, "Where is the God of justice?"
verses.3:1: "Behold, I am sending My messenger, and he shall clear the way before Me; and the Lord whom you seek shall suddenly come to His temple, even the Messenger of the covenant in whom you delight; behold, He is coming," says the LORD of hosts.
verses.3:2: Yet who can endure the day of His coming, and who shall stand when He appears? For He is like a refiner's fire and like fullers' lye.
verses.3:3: He shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver; He shall purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver, so that they shall present an offering to the LORD in righteousness.
verses.3:4: Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem shall be pleasing to the LORD, as in the days of old and as in ancient years.
verses.3:5: "Then I will draw near to you for judgment, and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, and against the adulterers, and against those who swear falsely, and against those who oppress the hired worker in his wages, the widow and the fatherless, and those who thrust aside the sojourner and do not fear Me," says the LORD of hosts.
verses.3:6: "For I, the LORD, have not changed; therefore you, O sons of Jacob, have not been consumed.
verses.3:7: From the days of your fathers you have turned aside from My statutes and have not kept them. Return to Me, and I will return to you," says the LORD of hosts. Yet you say, "In what way shall we return?"
verses.3:8: "Shall a man rob God? Yet you are robbing Me! But you say, 'How have we robbed You?' In the tithe and the contribution!
verses.3:9: You are cursed with a curse, for it is Me whom you are robbing—this entire nation!
verses.3:10: Bring the full tithe into the storehouse, that there may be food in My house; and test Me now in this," says the LORD of hosts, "if I will not open for you the windows of heaven and pour down for you a blessing until there is no more room to hold it.
verses.3:11: And I will rebuke the devourer for your sake, so that it shall not destroy the fruit of your ground; nor shall your vine in the field fail to bear its fruit," says the LORD of hosts.
verses.3:12: "And all the nations shall call you blessed, for you shall be a land of delight," says the LORD of hosts.
verses.3:13: "Your words have been harsh against Me," says the LORD. Yet you say, "What have we spoken against You?"
verses.3:14: "You have said, 'It is in vain to serve God; and what gain is it that we have kept His charge, and that we have walked as mourners before the LORD of hosts?
verses.3:15: And now we call the proud blessed; indeed, those who practice wickedness are built up; indeed, they even test God and escape!'"
verses.3:16: Then those who feared the LORD spoke one to another, and the LORD gave ear and heard; and a book of remembrance was written before Him for those who fear the LORD and who esteem His name.
verses.3:17: "They shall be Mine," says the LORD of hosts, "as My treasured possession on the day that I act; and I will spare them as a man spares his own son who serves him.
verses.3:18: Then you shall once more discern between the righteous and the wicked, between the one who serves God and the one who does not serve Him."
verses.3:19: "For behold, the day is coming, burning like a furnace; and all the proud, yes, every doer of wickedness, shall be stubble; and the day that is coming shall set them ablaze," says the LORD of hosts, "so that it will leave them neither root nor branch.
verses.3:20: But for you who fear My name, the sun of righteousness shall arise with healing in its wings; and you shall go forth and leap like calves from the stall.
verses.3:21: And you shall tread down the wicked, for they shall be ashes beneath the soles of your feet on the day that I act," says the LORD of hosts.
verses.3:22: "Behold, I am sending you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and awesome day of the LORD.
verses.3:23: And he shall turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the hearts of the children to their fathers, lest I come and strike the land with a decree of utter destruction."
verses.3:24: "Remember the law of Moses My servant, which I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel—the statutes and judgments."

notes.1:1: Oracle translates Hebrew massa, literally a burden or solemn prophetic pronouncement. The name Malachi means My messenger.
notes.1:13: Snort at it renders a Hebrew verb expressing contemptuous dismissal; ancient scribal tradition noted this clause among passages safeguarded for reverence toward God.
notes.2:3: Seed translates Hebrew zera, which can denote either sown grain or priestly offspring.
notes.2:12: Both him who wakes and him who answers translates a Hebrew merism expressing completeness, meaning every last person.
notes.2:15: The Hebrew phrasing of the opening clauses is unusually compressed and may alternatively be rendered, Did not the One make them, with a remnant of the Spirit belonging to Him?
notes.2:16: The Hebrew clause literally reads for he hates sending away, understood traditionally of the LORD's hatred of divorce, or alternatively of a man who hates and divorces his wife.
notes.3:1: My messenger echoes the prophet's name in 1:1, while the Messenger of the covenant stands in parallel with the Lord who comes suddenly to His temple.
notes.3:17: Treasured possession translates Hebrew segullah, the covenant term for Israel as the LORD's prized inheritance.
notes.3:24: In this Hebrew versification, chapter 3 extends through verse 24 and closes with the summons to remember the law of Moses.
